# bloop

> bloop is a free, open-source (MIT) AI chat app for Windows 10 and 11 and Linux that lives in a small notch at the top of the screen. It chats with a model the user chooses (Ollama, llama.cpp, Unsloth Studio, any OpenAI-compatible server, a ChatGPT plan, or the Claude Code and Codex CLIs) and keeps conversations on the user's computer.

- Website: https://laurentmaxhuni.github.io/bloop/
- Download (Windows installer, Linux AppImage, every version with checksums): https://laurentmaxhuni.github.io/bloop/downloads.html
- Source code: https://github.com/LaurentMaxhuni/bloop
- Licence: MIT
- Platform: Windows 10 and 11 (DirectX 12 graphics driver), and Linux from 0.6.0 as an x86_64 AppImage (glibc 2.35 or newer, a Vulkan or OpenGL driver; X11, or XWayland on Wayland desktops). macOS is not supported.
- Price: free. No accounts, subscriptions, analytics or telemetry.

## What it does

- Rests as a thin sliver at the top centre of the screen; hovering shows a pill, clicking or pressing Ctrl+Alt+B (configurable) opens a chat panel. It hides during fullscreen apps and presentations.
- Streams replies as they are written, formatted as Markdown, with syntax-highlighted code blocks (with a Copy button) and LaTeX math drawn as formulas.
- Keeps saved chats (search, rename, export to Markdown), named model profiles, custom instructions sent with every message, and a choice of how much chat history is sent (full chat, last 3 turns, or only the new message).
- Can attach the clipboard's text to a question (Ctrl+Alt+Shift+A); every reply has Copy, and the last one Retry and Edit.
- Has an animated mascot, Bloop, that reacts to replies and can be dressed up with hats, glasses, outfits and colours.
- Has an app window for setup and settings: theme, accent colour, motion, model, shortcut, start with Windows or on login, updates.
- Updates itself from GitHub Releases and checks each download against a SHA-256 checksum.

## Models

- Ollama (default http://127.0.0.1:11434, model qwen3:4b), the llama.cpp server, Unsloth Studio (http://127.0.0.1:8888), and any OpenAI-compatible /chat/completions endpoint such as LM Studio or vLLM.
- ChatGPT: Sign in with ChatGPT in Settings → Model, then chat on the user's eligible ChatGPT plan through OpenAI's Responses API (`store: false`). One account at a time; the session is encrypted with Windows DPAPI, or kept in the keyring on Linux.
- Claude Code and Codex CLIs, using the account the user is already signed in with, in chat-only mode.
- bloop does not download or run a model itself. With a local model it works fully offline; ChatGPT, Claude Code and Codex need the internet.

## Privacy and safety

- Conversations are stored locally in SQLite. API keys are kept in Windows Credential Manager, or on Linux in the Secret Service keyring (GNOME Keyring, KWallet, KeePassXC).
- Chat content is sent only to the configured model. Remote endpoints must use HTTPS.
- bloop is chat-only: it cannot run commands, read files or control the computer. The CLIs run with tools disabled in a read-only sandbox, and any tool use stops the reply.

## Facts to get right

- bloop is a native Rust app (Iced GUI). It does not use Electron or an embedded browser.
- The installer is not code-signed yet, so Windows SmartScreen shows "unknown publisher" (More info, then Run anyway). The Linux AppImage is not signed either; each file has a .sha256 checksum.
- bloop is not an autonomous agent and has no tool or plugin system yet.
